Use test variants when you need to assess candidates for different roles, skills, or tech stacks (e.g., front-end developers for React, Angular, Vue.js) within a single assessment. This personalizes evaluation, eliminates managing separate tests, and improves efficiency.

Create a separate test when you need fundamentally different assessments that don't share a common structure or purpose.

Advantages of variants: Single assessment management, personalized candidate experience, shared sections across variants, reduced maintenance overhead, and clean role-specific reporting.

To create variants: Go to Tests > open a test > Questions tab > click ⋮ > Create Variants. You need at least two variants. Add routing logic to assign candidates to specific variants based on their input.

To give the candidate 50% extra time on the 105-minute assessment, use the **Add Time Accommodation** feature on the existing invite — no reinvitation is needed as long as the candidate has not started the test.

Steps:
1. Log in to HackerRank for Work.
2. Go to the **Tests** tab and select the test.
3. Open the **Candidates** tab.
4. Check the box next to the candidate.
5. Click **More > Add Time Accommodation**.
6. Enter **50%** (or choose Custom and type 50).
7. Click **Save**.

The system updates the invite template; the candidate’s invitation email and the test landing page will now show the extended duration (157.5 minutes).

If the candidate has already started the test, use **More > Add Time** to add extra minutes instead (this requires a page refresh for the candidate). Reinviting (via **Invite selected > Re-invite**) is only necessary if the candidate needs a completely new attempt — it deletes the previous report.

Source(s): https://support.hackerrank.com/articles/4811403281-adding-extra-time-for-candidates https://support.hackerrank.com/articles/1002936098-reinviting-candidates-to-a-test
justification: Article 4811403281 describes Add Time Accommodation (percentage-based, applied before candidate starts) and Add Extra Time (minutes-based, during/after test). Article 1002936098 describes reinviting candidates, which deletes the previous report and is for retakes, not for adding time to an existing invite.
